Question: For each positive integer \(n,\) let \(S(n)\) denote the sum of the digits of \(n.\) For how many values of \(n\) is \(n+S(n)+S(S(n))=2007?\)
Solution:
Digit sums are small, so the equation forces \(n\) close to \(2007\). Both digit sums are positive, giving \(n\le2005\). For numbers below \(2007\), the largest digit sum is \(28\), attained at \(1999\). A number from \(1\) through \(28\) has digit sum at most \(10\). Therefore
\[
1969=2007-28-10\le n\le2005.
\]
The endpoint \(1969\) gives \(1969+25+7=2001\), so it is not a solution. Also, for \(1990\le n\le1999\), we have \(S(n)\ge19\), making the total at least \(1990+19+1=2010\). We only need the following three blocks.

For \(n=1970+u\), where \(0\le u\le9\) is an integer, \(S(n)=17+u\). When \(u\le2\), its digit sum is \(8+u\); when \(u\ge3\), it is \(u-1\). Thus
\[
n+S(n)+S(S(n))=
\begin{cases}
1995+3u,&0\le u\le2,\\
1986+3u,&3\le u\le9.
\end{cases}
\]
Setting these equal to \(2007\) gives \(u=4\), outside the first range, or \(u=7\), valid in the second. This yields \(n=1977\).

For \(n=1980+u\), \(S(n)=18+u\). Its digit sum changes form at \(u=2\), giving
\[
n+S(n)+S(S(n))=
\begin{cases}
2007+3u,&0\le u\le1,\\
1998+3u,&2\le u\le9.
\end{cases}
\]
The solutions are \(u=0\) and \(u=3\), yielding \(1980\) and \(1983\).

Finally, for \(n=2000+u\), with \(0\le u\le5\), both digit sums equal \(2+u\). The equation becomes \(2004+3u=2007\), so \(u=1\), yielding \(2001\).

The four candidates satisfy the original equation:
\[
\begin{aligned}
1977+24+6&=2007,\\
1980+18+9&=2007,\\
1983+21+3&=2007,\\
2001+3+3&=2007.
\end{aligned}
\]
The disjoint blocks exhaust the bounded interval, so there are exactly \(\boxed{4}\) solutions, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
